title: Vibe-coded a Windows 11 frontend for Hunyuan3D this weekend
author: Acceptable-Budget658
selftext:
I spent the weekend building Galatea, a small Windows 11 desktop app for running a local Hunyuan3D image-to-3D workflow with a more visual interface.

It handles image selection, presets, progress logs, WSL setup checks, Blender export, and previews the generated model inside the app. Still rough, but it’s already generating GLB/FBX outputs from images.

Sharing a quick video because 

I’m honestly pretty happy with how far this got in a weekend. Curious what people think.

comments.author: Acceptable-Budget658
comments.body: Obs: bad choice of a model to show off, I know lol

comments.author: syn_krown
comments.body: Thats cool! Does running local mean no API cost?

replies.author: Acceptable-Budget658
replies.body:
Exactly! A friend of mine told me about meshy.ai, I tested it and I was really impressed by the results (not promoting them or anything). Then I looked up for open source models that could run locally on my GTX 4070. 

I tested SF3D, really cheap on the GPU requirements, but not so good results. I didn't find a way to input multiple images for it to render, so the image has to be in a perfect 3/4 perspective, otherwise it creates a 3D "plate" with your image on it. It creates the shape AND the texture in one process though, so that's something I guess. 

Later on I found out about Hunyuan3D, tweaked it with 33 different attempts (changing shape and texture parameters and checking the results), and finally got a good default settings, that I made as standard on Galatea.

Oh, since it uses CUDA threads, I didn't find a way to make it run on AMD GPUs but I'll share all of it on a GitHub repository, if anyone likes it and wants to test it.
